title: Task 6: keep the inputs but change the rule
notes: 2 minutes / practice. Teaching intent: Task 6: keep the inputs but change the rule. Define: An input-only monitor can miss a changed input-output relationship. Walk through: Replace 2*x0 with -2*x0 in the synthetic target. Keep the exact test inputs, their order, noise realization and all model parameters fixed. Ask: Which observations would reveal this change? Expected answer and boundary: Outcome labels and the errors against them. Here an input histogram is exactly unchanged by construction; this does not prove that every possible target change always worsens every metric. Visual purpose: show Same X and noise > Change x0 coefficient > Same model predictions > New outcomes. title: Compare two different kinds of change
notes: 2 minutes / practice. Teaching intent: Compare two different kinds of change. Define: Input shift changes the cases; concept shift changes the relationship. Walk through: Show identical input hashes for Task 6 and compare its actual errors with the original test. For Task 5 show the declared x1 scaling and unchanged target rule. Ask: Can an unchanged input histogram certify model accuracy? Expected answer and boundary: No. It cannot see this constructed conditional change. Delayed or selectively available real outcomes also require care; input and outcome monitoring answer different questions. Visual purpose: show Task 5: inputs changed | Task 6: relationship changed | Model fixed in both. title: Task 7: ask what one input change does
notes: 2 minutes / practice. Teaching intent: Task 7: ask what one input change does. Define: Predict a function change before calling predict. Walk through: The helper reports the raw x0 slope. For these additive models, increasing x0 by 0.5 changes the prediction by 0.5 times that slope, holding every other coordinate fixed. Ask: Is this a physical intervention or a new accuracy test? Expected answer and boundary: Neither. It is an exact check of the fitted mathematical function. It uses no new target labels and does not establish physical causation. Visual purpose: show Original row > Add 0.5 to x0 > Same fitted function > Prediction difference.
